hero.lead: Free up storage, understand memory usage, monitor running apps, check battery health and see important information about your Mac — from one simple dashboard. You review everything. Nothing is permanently deleted.

coreFeatures.title: Eight cleaning tools. One calm interface.
coreFeatures.intro: Each tool shows what it found, why it’s there and what happens if you remove it — so you can clean with confidence instead of guesswork.

scanDemo.intro: Smart Clean looks through caches, logs, app leftovers, developer tools and your Downloads in one pass, then sorts what it finds into plain-language groups — each one split into what’s safe to clean and what deserves a second look.
scanDemo.canFreeUp: Your Mac can free up {{total}} GB
scanDemo.safeSummary: {{amount}} GB is safe to clean right away. The rest is yours to review.
scanDemo.footNote: Example scan using the app’s sample data. Results on your Mac will differ.

performanceMonitor.intro: MacBook Cleaner is more than a storage cleaner. The Performance tab shows how your Mac is doing right now — in plain language, without turning into a developer tool.
performanceMonitor.shotAlt: MacBook Cleaner Performance dashboard showing CPU, memory, storage and battery gauges, a Mac Health summary and live charts
performanceMonitor.shotNote: Shown with the app’s sample data. On your Mac, every value is read live from macOS.

runningApps.intro: Running Apps lists what’s open on your Mac with its memory, CPU and how long it’s been running. Helper processes count toward their app, so a browser with dozens of tabs shows one honest total.
checks: Sort by memory, CPU, running time or name
Apps by default — background and system processes only if you ask
Memory uses the same measure as Activity Monitor
runningApps.note: Example values for illustration — not benchmarks.

battery.title: Understand your battery.
battery.intro: On MacBooks, see exactly what macOS knows about your battery — no guesswork, no invented scores.
checks: Cycle count — the number of full charge cycles completed
Maximum capacity compared with when it was new
Battery condition, as shown in System Settings
battery.finePrint: MacBook Cleaner reports battery information; it can’t repair or improve a battery’s physical health. Desktop Macs simply don’t show this section.

macInfo.intro: Model, chip, memory, storage, displays, macOS version and uptime — in one dashboard instead of five different places. MacBook Cleaner also shows whether macOS’s own update check found an update, with a shortcut to Software Update.
macInfo.finePrint: Read locally from macOS and never uploaded. Your serial number isn’t read at all.

howItWorks.title: Four steps. You’re in charge of every one.

steps.title: Scan your Mac
steps.body: One click checks caches, logs, developer tools, apps, Downloads and your largest files — all on your Mac.

steps.title: Review recommendations
steps.body: Items are labeled Safe or Review, with a plain explanation of what each one is. Untick anything you want to keep.

steps.title: Move to Trash
steps.body: Confirm, and the items you approved go to the Trash. Your own files always need an extra confirmation.

steps.title: Reclaim storage
steps.body: Changed your mind? Put anything back from the Trash. When you’re sure, empty it to get the space back.

storageSection.intro: MacBook Cleaner measures your real folders and shows them as one colorful storage ring — the same categories you see in the app.
checks: Sizes in decimal gigabytes, the way macOS reports storage
Space that can’t be attributed is labeled honestly as System Data
Libraries like Photos are measured, never opened or picked apart

storageViz.diskAriaLabel: Example disk: {{used}} GB used, {{free}} GB free, {{recoverable}} GB potentially recoverable after review
storageViz.defaultNote: Illustrative example using the app’s sample data — your Mac’s numbers will be different. Hover or focus a category for details.

applications.label: Applications
applications.note: Apps plus leftovers from apps you’ve removed

documents.label: Documents
documents.note: Documents and Desktop — reviewed, never preselected

photos.label: Photos
photos.note: Your Photos library is sized, never touched

downloads.label: Downloads
downloads.note: Old installers, disk images and archives

cache.label: Cache
cache.note: App and browser caches that rebuild themselves

other.label: Other
other.note: Music, mail, messages and other app data

system-data.label: System Data
system-data.note: macOS and space not attributable to a folder

safeCleaning.intro: Cleaning tools need deep access to your disk. MacBook Cleaner is built so that a mistake is hard to make — and easy to undo.

safe.label: Safe
safe.title: Rebuilds itself
safe.body: Caches and logs your apps re-create on their own. Preselected for you.

review.label: Review
review.title: Worth a look first
review.body: Things that may hold state you care about. Never preselected.

protected.label: Protected
protected.title: Can’t be selected
protected.body: Anything that looks like a backup, keychain or key — refused by the app’s native safety layer.

principles.title: Review before anything is removed
principles.body: Every cleanup shows exactly what will be moved and asks you to confirm.

principles.title: Trash first, always
principles.body: Items go to the Trash — never permanently deleted. The app never empties your Trash.

principles.title: Your files are your call
principles.body: Downloads, Desktop, Documents and Movies are never preselected and always need an extra confirmation.

principles.title: Guardrails that can’t be bypassed
principles.body: A native check refuses system folders, your home folder, its main folders and anything outside your home folder.

principles.title: “Never suggest this again”
principles.body: Exclude any file or folder and it won’t be suggested again — manually or on a schedule.

principles.title: No surprise automation
principles.body: Automatic cleaning is off by default, needs explicit consent, and only touches six developer caches.

beforeAfter.title: From “where did it all go?” to “oh, that’s where.”
beforeAfter.intro: Drag the handle to compare. MacBook Cleaner doesn’t make your disk bigger — it makes it understandable, so recovering space is a decision instead of a guess.
beforeList: Storage bar says “System Data” and little else
Large files buried deep inside folders
Caches and logs piling up unnoticed
Old installers and disk images in Downloads
No idea what’s safe to remove
afterList: Biggest files listed first, with Quick Look
Caches grouped and marked Safe or Review
Downloads sorted by age and type
Space recovered on your terms — via the Trash

privacyBand.title: Your files stay on your Mac.
privacyBand.lead: A cleaner needs deep access to your disk. That’s exactly why MacBook Cleaner is built to need your trust as little as possible.

points.title: Scanned on your Mac
points.body: Every scan and every cleanup runs locally. There’s no cloud service involved.

points.title: Nothing is uploaded
points.body: No analytics, telemetry or crash reporting. Your files, running apps, battery and Mac details never leave your Mac.

points.title: No account needed to try it
points.body: No sign-up, no email, no credit card — download it and your free trial starts. Buying a lifetime license later only needs the key from your purchase, never a new account.

points.title: Contents stay unread
points.body: The app looks at sizes and dates. File contents are only read to confirm two files are exact duplicates.

privacyBand.permissionsHeading: What macOS may ask you to allow — and why

permissions.title: Downloads, Desktop & Documents
permissions.body: macOS asks before the app can look in these folders, so it can find large files and old downloads.

permissions.title: Control Finder
permissions.body: Asked the first time you clean. The app asks Finder to move items to the Trash, so “Put Back” works.

permissions.title: Full Disk Access — optional
permissions.body: Lets the app measure locations macOS keeps private, like some caches and the Trash. It works without it.

permissions.title: Notifications — optional
permissions.body: Only for scheduled-cleanup reminders and summaries.

privacyBand.footNote: You can review or revoke any of these in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
